slides.title: Which short track blade should you buy?
slides.sub: Flex, length, steel and fit, explained

slides.title: Flex decides how the blade feels
slides.body: A flexible blade moves with your push and forgives small technique errors. A stiffer blade returns energy directly and holds a firm line.

slides.title: Match length to your boot and style
slides.body: Shorter blades change direction quickly and feel lively. Longer blades track straighter and carry more speed on the straights.

slides.title: Harder steel holds an edge longer
slides.body: Bimetal runners, around 62 HRC, balance performance and value. Full PM steel, around 64 HRC, stays sharp longer between sharpenings.

slides.title: Check your mounting spacing first
slides.body: Short track boots use 165 mm spacing. Inline boots are often drilled at 195 mm. An adapter set bridges the gap using the existing holes, with no drilling.

slides.title: Spacing first, then cup height
slides.caption: Match the hole spacing, then pick a cup height: lower feels more stable, higher lets you lean deeper.

slides.text: Flow or hold, that is the whole question.
